title: Solution controls
_comment: The algorithm blocks are form-editable; `solvers` and `relaxationFactors`
are not, and that is deliberate.
`solvers` is keyed by equation — p, U, k, alpha.water — so its shape is the
case's, not something a schema can name in advance. Same for
`relaxationFactors`. Both are preserved and edited in the text tab.
Which algorithm block a case has depends on its solver: SIMPLE for steady,
PISO and PIMPLE for transient. No field here is required, so the form shows
the block the case actually has and stays silent about the others — a
required key would report a steady case as missing PIMPLE settings it has
Keys were taken from what the corpus contains, in frequency order.

fields.label: SIMPLE: non-orthogonal correctors
fields.help: Extra pressure solves per iteration. Raise it on a mesh with high non-orthogonality.

fields.label: SIMPLE: consistent (SIMPLEC)
fields.help: Allows much larger relaxation factors, and usually converges in fewer iterations.

fields.label: SIMPLE: reference cell
fields.help: Pins pressure in a closed domain, where otherwise only its gradient is determined.

fields.label: PIMPLE: outer correctors
fields.help: 1 makes PIMPLE behave as PISO. Above 1 it iterates within each time step, which allows a larger step.

fields.label: PIMPLE: momentum predictor
fields.help: Usually off for low-Reynolds or strongly buoyant flows.
